name: Fluorouracil + Mitomycin with concurrent radiation (definitive anal SCC)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.histology: squamous cell carcinoma of the anus
biomarkers.note: Definitive concurrent chemoradiation with fluorouracil plus mitomycin (the Nigro-type regimen) is organ-preserving standard of care for localized anal squamous cell carcinoma. There is no routine molecular biomarker gate for regimen selection; DPYD testing is advised before fluoropyrimidine exposure. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Anal Carcinoma, ANAL-B (Systemic Therapy Regimens and Dosing - Localized Cancer).

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Give per emetogenicity on chemotherapy days concurrent with radiation.

supportiveCare: Single definitive concurrent chemoradiation course (NOT a repeating cycle): chemotherapy is delivered on days 1 to 4 / 29 to 32 within one radiation course; cycleLengthDays (42) encodes the approximately 6-week concurrent course and cycles is 1.
Fluoropyrimidine DPYD testing per FDA boxed warning before starting (ANAL footnote a).
Monitor for radiation dermatitis/proctitis and mitomycin myelosuppression during the concurrent course.
monitoring: CBC before each chemotherapy administration and during nadir (mitomycin/5-FU myelosuppression)
renal function and signs of hemolytic-uremic syndrome / thrombotic microangiopathy (mitomycin)
response assessment (clinical exam; imaging) after chemoradiation

doseModificationRules.text: Adjust the second chemotherapy administration (days 29 to 32 / day 29) for cytopenias per protocol; obtain clinical review.
Reduce dose or avoid fluorouracil in DPYD-deficient patients per FDA boxed warning; clinical review required.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (continuous infusion)
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Anal v2.2026, ANAL-B (anal line 531). Fluorouracil 1000 mg/m2/day by continuous IV infusion on days 1 to 4 and 29 to 32, concurrent with radiation. DPYD: FDA boxed warning recommends testing for DPYD genetic variants before starting a fluoropyrimidine; dose-reduce or avoid in DPYD-deficient patients (ANAL footnote a). No ISMP tall-man form.

provenance.locator: ANAL-B (Continuous infusion Fluorouracil 1000 mg/m2/day IV Days 1 to 4 and 29 to 32); anal line 531

drugs.name: mitomycin
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Anal v2.2026, ANAL-B (anal line 532). mitomycin 10 mg/m2 IV bolus on days 1 and 29, each dose capped at 20 mg, concurrent with radiation. ALTERNATIVE source-stated schedule: mitomycin 12 mg/m2 IV bolus on day 1 only, capped at 20 mg (anal line 535). ISMP: 'mitomycin' is on the ISMP list of confused drug names (distinguish from mitoXANTRONE). CUMULATIVE TOXICITY: mitomycin carries risk of cumulative and delayed myelosuppression and of hemolytic-uremic syndrome / thrombotic microangiopathy and pulmonary toxicity; the per-dose cap (20 mg) and limited number of doses in this regimen mitigate cumulative exposure.

provenance.locator: ANAL-B (Mitomycin 10 mg/m2 IV bolus Days 1 and 29, capped at 20 mg, with RT); anal line 532
